title: Single asset real estate: the 90-day deadline before a secured lender gets stay relief
rule: Single asset real estate is one property or project, other than residential property with fewer than 4 units, generating substantially all gross income of a debtor, not a family farmer, that conducts no substantial business on it besides operating it. A secured creditor that asks is entitled to stay relief unless, by the later of 90 days after the order for relief (extendable within it for cause) or 30 days after the court finds the debtor subject to this rule, the debtor files a plan with a reasonable possibility of confirmation within a reasonable time or starts monthly payments of nondefault contract-rate interest on the value of the creditor's interest.
changeWatch: Amendments to 11 U.S.C. 101(51B) or 362(d)(3); the definition has had no debt ceiling since 2005, when a $4,000,000 secured-debt limit was struck; Pub. L. 119-27 makes a conforming change to 362(d)(3)(B)(ii) when its new 362(d)(5) takes effect (by January 18, 2027 at the latest).
